summary: Wingspan is a smooth engine-building card game where players attract birds into three habitat rows, chaining bird powers to generate food, lay eggs, and draw more cards each round. It's approachable and gorgeous, playing mostly in parallel with only occasional bumps into other players via powers that trigger off what another player does.
praised: gorgeous art and bird theme that appeals broadly
satisfying, tactile engine-building with real combo moments
smooth rules for the depth of the tableau-building genre
great solo mode and wide table appeal across experience levels
criticised: mostly solitaire/parallel play with limited direct interaction
bird-power variance can make some hands feel stronger than others
the birdfeeder dice can occasionally swing food availability
end-game bonus card scoring can feel disconnected from the birds themselves

interaction.kind: mostly parallel engine-building with a shared bird tray
interaction.detail: Each player builds their own habitat rows independently, with almost no ability to touch an opponent's tableau directly. The only shared elements are the central bird tray and birdfeeder dice, where taking a bird or food resource can leave less for the next player.

subsystems: bird tableau engine across forest, grassland and wetland habitats
scoring.how_you_win: Over four rounds players play birds into a habitat network, gaining food, laying eggs, and drawing cards through that engine; whoever has accumulated the most points from bird cards, eggs, cached food, tucked cards, bonus cards, and round goals at the end wins.
